answer: An agent economy resists sybils by pricing identity creation: every new account must lock a small refundable bond before it can trade, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs real capital instead of being free. Genuine agents earn that bond back through verified work, while clones that never complete anything stay stuck, each isolated like an island with no bridge to shared reputation. Real activity forms a dense nebula of linked, checkable transactions; a sybil farm shows only a thin delta of shallow actions that never deepen into trust.
